title: Marina Cove concierge workflow onramp - scratch
content:
Objective: capture intake call + immediate engineering concerns for Marina Cove (luxury-hospitality concierge). They want an assistant that can handle reservations, upsells, local recommendations, and payments (tokenized), with tight latency and PCI constraints. Notes below are an unpolished working list — use for PoC planning and sizing.

Call summary (2025-01-10):
- Participants: Marina Cove: Jenna Park (CTO), Omar Haddad (Head of Ops), Naomi Lee (Security lead). Redwood: Aisha, Liam.
- Use case: Hotel concierge chat (web + mobile) + voice later. Core flows: book/reschedule reservations, recommend nearby experiences, upsell services, process payment tokens (not raw CC storage in app), attach itinerary to profile, export receipts.
- Expected traffic: pilot ~5 hotels, ~20 concurrent sessions peak (evening), target production ~500 concurrent sessions during promotional windows. Peak request estimate ~20–30 req/s, average request ~120–200 tokens, occasional long system prompts for context (session history up to 2k tokens).
- SLOs: target p50 latency <250ms for text gen, p95 <600ms. Absolute business constraint: any payment-required flow must finish within 3s end-to-end (including API calls).
- Compliance: PCI scope mandatory, GDPR data residency EU for EU hotels. They prefer VPC/private deployment with customer-managed KMS/HSM.

Technical requirements / asks:
- Private control plane with VPC peering into Marina Cove cloud account, optional on-prem gateway for payment vaulting.
- KMS/HSM integration for tokenization; keys must never leave customer control.
- Per-tenant telemetry (token counts, cost, latencies) exposed in console, with role-based access (ops vs finance).
- Session affinity and KV cache for user conversation state to reduce repeated context tokens. Need eviction policy for long-running sessions (30d TTL?).
- Function/tool calls: must support synchronous callouts to reservation API and payment token exchange. Need safe-fallback behavior if payment provider fails (e.g., queue and notify).
- Moderation/Pii redaction pre-send for customer-supplied attachments (addresses, phone).

Gotchas / open risks (brain dump):
- PCI scoping: Redwood-hosted tokenization would increase scope; customer insists tokenization in their environment. We'll need to validate our flow with Security early.
- KMS integration variations across clouds (AWS KMS vs cloud HSM) — POC will need a diagram showing key flow.
- Latency: VPC routing + KMS calls could add 50–200ms; combined model inference + API call could blow p95 target. Consider collocating KMS and inference region.
- KV cache growth: concierge sessions often accumulate lots of context (itinerary history, preferences). Need strategy: summarize older turns, store embeddings only, or external session store. This affects memory usage on runtime pods.
- Cost sensitivity: CX team expects hosted-like pay-as-you-go pricing for pilot, but infra team favors reserved capacity for production. Need clear cost estimates for both.
- Tooling for rollback: if model update affects correctness of reservation flows, they require canary + strict validation on sample prompts.
- Multiregion data residency: EU hotels require EU-only storage/keys. Must ensure routing policy respects tenancy and SLOs.

Model/workload considerations:
- Suggested model variants for PoC: a smaller fast model for core deterministic flows (slot-filling, confirmations) and a larger LLM for recommendations/upsell. E.g., openchat-medium for confirmations + openchat-large for recommendations.
- Quantization allowed for latency; but need to validate behavioral regressions on regression suite (booking confirmations).
- Streaming not required for payment flows; prefer synchronous reliable response.

Immediate next steps (owner / ETA):
- Aisha: create PoC spec doc with architecture diagram and initial cost estimate (due 2025-01-17).
- Liam: draft network/KMS integration diagram + list of required infra permissions for Marina Cove cloud account (due 2025-01-15).
- Marco: assemble prompt test set for reservation flows (10 canonical dialogs + edge cases) and basic eval script. Start data scrub process for sample conversations (due 2025-01-20).
- Sales: schedule 1-week PoC kickoff with Marina Cove and share NDA + minimal data requirements (contact: Jenna Park).
- Create JIRA ticket (JIRA-2247) to track infra tasks and compliance sign-off.

POC scope proposal (rough):
- Duration: 2 weeks + 1 week observation.
- Env: Private deployment in Marina Cove AWS account (single region), 2-node Dedicated pool (2x80GB GPUs) for initial throughput, local KMS integration via AWS KMS with CMK in customer's account.
- Deliverables: working concierge demo, performance report (latency/cost per flow), regression tests for booking confirmations, short ops runbook for incident handling.

Questions to resolve / items to escalate:
- Can Marina Cove accept Redwood-managed keys for the PoC or insist on customer-managed KMS from day 1? (security vs friction)
- Confirm exact residency list (which hotels in EU vs US) to plan routing.
- Clarify SLA expectations for pilot vs prod and whether SLA needs to include payment flows.

Loose notes / prompts / quick ideas:
- Implement a 2-tier model routing rule: if flow contains 'payment' or 'reservation' -> route to deterministic fast model; else -> route to recommendation model. Use token-level cost tracking per route.
- Consider prefix caching for standard confirmation templates to shave tokens.
- Instrument latent KV sizes per session and trigger server-side summarization job when > 2k tokens.

Raw snippets from call (verbatim-ish):
- Jenna: "We cannot have card numbers in transit in Redwood storage — keys must be ours."
- Omar: "If the assistant screws up a booking, we need easy human-in-the-loop correction and audit trail."

Notes-to-self: prioritize compliance diagram and KMS perms; get Security review before infra work. Use small model for deterministic tasks to reduce p95 and token cost.

-- end scratch --
